title: Hidden Materials May Help Batteries and Solar Fuels
summary:
When scientists heat chemicals to make a new solid, they often look only at the final product. A new study says the short stages in the middle can matter too.

Researchers watched starter molecules change as they got hotter. They found forms of materials that normal methods can miss. The work was reported in Nature Communications.

One find was a new form of bismuth vanadate called β-BiVO4. Regular BiVO4 is studied for using sunlight to help make clean hydrogen fuel. The new form has a different structure and reacts to light in a new way.

Another middle-stage material could store a lot of lithium, which is useful for batteries. Dr. Sebastian Pike said the steps between start and finish can be useful on their own.
why_it_matters: New materials can help make cleaner energy and better batteries for everyday devices.
